hints_cache: Since we are building a count based on the string's length, this fits the Dynamic Programming pattern. Think about how the total number of unique subsequences grows as you process the string one letter at a time from left to right.

If every character in the string were unique, each new letter would double your current count (because you can either add the new letter to every existing subsequence or not) and add itself as a new single-letter subsequence.

When characters repeat, the 'doubling' logic overcounts. Specifically, when you see a letter for the second time, you are recreating all the subsequences that were already counted the last time that same letter appeared.

To fix the overcounting, you need to keep track of the 'added value' from each letter's previous occurrence. An array of size 26 can store the total count of subsequences we had just before each letter was last processed.

The core logic: current total = (previous total * 2) - (total just before the last time we saw this character). Don't forget to add 1 for the new character itself or handle the 'empty' subsequence case carefully, and apply the modulo at every step.
